title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The ambient project, from context, is a description of the moduli of elliptic curves over S above S_0 = Spec Z[1/2] through the Legendre form y^2 = x(x-1)(x-λ). In that picture the modular base is U_{0,3} = P^1 minus {0,1,∞} (the λ-line), and the groups are μ_4, μ_2 and S_3. The machine transcription renders μ as 'H' or 'M'; the next page's (μ4×S3)_S confirms the reading.

Previous page. For E/S, Grothendieck defines two μ_4-torsors.
- L_{E/S}: the torsor of 'épi-rigidifications de Legendre', i.e. isomorphisms K : Δ_{E/S} ≅ O_Σ(1)_t^♮.
- Q_{E/S}: the torsor of isomorphisms K' : Δ_{E/S} ≅ O_Σ(1)_t whose square, read as an isomorphism T ≅ T ∧^{±1} ω_J, comes from a section of the μ_2-torsor ω_J.

This page.
- (42) Q_{E/S} is a 'combinatorial' torsor whose μ_2-quotient (pushout along μ4 → μ4/μ2 ≅ μ2) is ω_J: Q_{E/S}/μ_2 ≅ ω_J.
- (43) There is a canonical isomorphism of μ_4-torsors Q_{E/S} ∧^{μ4} Q_{0S} ≅ L_{E/S}. Here Q_0 is a fixed universal μ_4-torsor over the base. Equivalently, L_{E/S} ≅ Isom_{μ4-tors}(Q_0^{-1}, Q_{E/S}).
- Remark: one could have defined Legendre épi-glyphes as trivialisations of Q rather than of L. The cost would be a less immediate relation with Jacobi épi-glyphes.
- (44) Taking μ_2-quotients of (43) gives L_{E/S}/μ_2 = L ∧^{μ4} μ_2 ≅ μ_4^* ∧ ω_J. Here μ_4^* is the scheme of primitive 4th roots of unity, a μ_2-torsor, and it equals Q_0/μ_2. So the μ_2-torsor associated with L is 'canonical': it depends only on ω_J.

Next page. Jacobi épi-glyphes of order 2 (orderings of the 2-torsion, or of the roots e_i) form an S_3-torsor. The 'bi-quadratic' structures then form a (μ4×S3)-torsor. This yields an action of μ4×S3 on U_{0,3}×μ_4^* and on the line bundle O(1):
- S_3 acts tautologically on λ, with a sign-character correction on μ_4^*;
- μ_4 acts through μ_4 → μ_2 on μ_4^*.

Purpose. The page is bookkeeping of torsors. It shows that the Legendre-rigidification torsor factors as a 'curve-dependent' part Q_{E/S} twisted by a universal constant torsor Q_0. That presents the moduli of Legendre-rigidified curves as U_{0,3}×μ_4^* with an explicit μ4×S3 symmetry.
errors: No mathematical error is visible, but the notation is idiosyncratic: ω_J, Q_0 and O(1)^♮ are defined on other pages.
(42) is stated without proof. The phrase 'schéma des diagonales' (reading uncertain) is unexplained here.
In (44) the factor written μ_4^* must be understood as the μ_2-torsor of primitive 4th roots of unity (μ_2 acting by ±1). It is not the dual group.

ideas.what: Decomposing a μ4-torsor of Legendre rigidifications as the contracted product of a curve-dependent torsor Q_{E/S} with a universal torsor Q_0, equivalently as Isom(Q_0^{-1}, Q_{E/S}).
ideas.modern_name: Contracted product / twisting of torsors; torsor of rigidifications in moduli problems
ideas.where_published: General torsor formalism in SGA/Giraud; this specific Legendre application is unpublished as far as known

ideas.what: The μ2-quotient of the Legendre torsor is canonical, ≅ μ_4^* ∧ ω_J (pushout along squaring μ4→μ2).
ideas.modern_name: Change of structure group along μ4 → μ2; Kummer-type torsor

ideas.what: Action of μ4×S3 on λ-line × μ_4^* (S3 tautologically on P^1 minus {0,1,∞} with a sign twist on μ_4^*) to describe the moduli of elliptic curves in char ≠ 2 via Legendre form.
ideas.modern_name: Legendre/λ-line presentation of M_{1,1}[1/2] as a quotient stack of Y(2) by S3 (and automorphism group extensions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Legendre, Jacobi); stack-theoretic versions Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur, later expositions

missed.claim: This is an explicit, torsor-theoretic account of the μ4-extension in the Legendre presentation of elliptic moduli over Z[1/2], with a canonical μ2-part ≅ μ_4^* ∧ ω_J. It is a careful stack-level bookkeeping of the sign twist in the S3 action on the λ-line, belonging to his 1980s anabelian/Teichmüller-tower work on M_{1,1}. It is probably known in substance (the Legendre stack is folklore) but not written in this form.
missed.quote: On voit aussitôt que les épi-glyphes de Legendre forment les sections d'un torseur sous μ4, tel que le μ2-torseur associé soit canonique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal. It could serve as a clean reference for the arithmetic structure (twists by μ_4^*, i.e. by Q(i)) of the Legendre family over Z[1/2], relevant to Galois actions on π1 of P^1 minus 3 points versus M_{1,1}.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine torsor manipulation inside an unpublished, detailed treatment of Legendre-form moduli. The content is essentially known folklore. The only point of interest is the careful identification of the canonical μ2-part involving μ_4^*.
transcription_corrections: 'H_4', 'H_2', 'M_4' throughout should read μ_4, μ_2 (Grothendieck's handwritten μ).
'forment les motifs[?] d'un torseur' should probably read 'forment les sections d'un torseur'.
'(H_4)_S-torseurs' should read (μ_4)_S-torseurs; 'isomorphisme canonique' is the correct reading of the insertion.
'Q*_{0S}^{-1}' is the inverse μ4-torsor Q_{0S}^{-1}, and 'H^*_4' in (44) is μ_4^* (primitive 4th roots of unity).
'épi-glyphes de Jacobi d'ordre 4' at line end: the reading 'ordre 4' is plausible but the digit is uncertain.
